jobs.title: Business Operations Manager (1 Year Contract) (26-27)
jobs.description:
Description

BUSINESS OPERATIONS MANAGER

Position Summary

The Business Operations Manager (BOM) is responsible for the management of the school’s core business functions - accounting, HR, facilities and technology - as well as managing and overseeing day-to-day operations in the front office, including maintaining a pristine office space and welcoming and directing current and prospective families, students and guests. The BOM is a multi-talented leader who maintains and optimizes school systems, owns and is accountable for key school and campus processes like procurement and facilities maintenance, and partners with the Director of School Operations and School Leader to ensure our schools are well-run, fully compliant and financially secure, during both in-person and virtual learning.

The Business Operations Manager reports to the Director of School Operations and works closely with the Regional Operations, Accounting, HR, Facilities and Technology teams, the School Operations team, and School Leadership.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience:

Deep integrity and commitment to KIPP Public Schools Northern California’s mission and values required
2+ years of office management, operations, accounting, human resources or facilities management, including working knowledge of general office business systems and practices required
Experience working in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment required

Education:

Bachelor’s Degree and 2+ years of work experience or 4+ years’ work experience required

Knowledge/skills required:

Self-awareness and a commitment to continuous learning
Adept at problem solving and decision making, with a keen attention to detail
Ability to self-direct, prioritize and multi-task among competing goals
Demonstrated ability to work well with others and build relationships across teams
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with keen attention to detail
Proficiency in one or more of the the languages spoken by the school community (Spanish, Mandarin, Vietnamese), required/preferred
Proficiency in Microsoft Office suite or Google Suite required
Ability to learn and utilize technology necessary to operate in a virtual office environment (i.e. Zoom)

Essential Functions And Responsibilities

Manages daily office operations

Organizes, secures, and maintains a pristine office space and environment for students, staff and families
Models, upholds and maintains a positive, nurturing, achievement-oriented school culture by welcoming and attending to prospective and current families and directing phone calls and guests warmly and professionally
Drafts, translates, and distributes school correspondence and communications - including letters, newsletters and weekly bulletins - and manages or supports all other school-based communications and systems (ex. MailChimp, ParentSquare).
Partners with Director of School Operations, teachers and staff to plan and coordinate field trips and other student and school-wide events, as needed
Administers basic first aid, distributes medication, maintains injury reports, and contacts parents regarding health and safety, as necessary. Reports major injuries, head injuries and other school incidents to DSO.
Adhere to KIPP’s health and safety guidelines as outlined by the CDC, CDE, and public health agencies’ recommendations.

Oversees day-to-day accounting, contracting and vendor management procedures

Partner with the regional Accounting team to manage and oversee school-wide procurement, cash receipts, deposits, and the effective, compliant development and implementation of financial policies, including those related to accounts receivable and payable, budget line item management and invoice entry and approval.
Partner with the Director of School Operations and School Leader on schoolwide budget management, ensuring the school maintains at least a break-even budget at the end of the year.
Develops a strategy to source and select suppliers to ensure the school meets all federal, state and regional requirements related to purchasing, procurement and contracting; manage relationships with external vendors and ensure compliance (ex. nutrition, etc.)
Partner with the regional Facilities team to manage all on-campus maintenance and facilities issues, including managing relationships with vendors responsible for maintenance, janitorial and pest control.

Ensures compliance with all school and regional HR policies and procedures

Partner with the regional Human Resources team to inform and implement human resource (HR) management policies at the school, ensure staff have a clear understanding of HR policies and procedures and drive school-level compliance with relevant employment and labor laws.
Manage the administration of school personnel matters, including issues related to payroll, benefits, insurances, legal and other compliance matters, performance management, discipline, and staff grievances, and elevate major issues to the regional HR team when necessary.
Assist school team with the hiring, development and appraisal of non-teaching staff.
Maintain confidential staff records in accordance with KIPP Bay Area policies.
Manage and oversee substitute teacher coverage, communicating expectations to staff, securing coverage when staff are absent and managing substitute teachers while they are on campus.

Serve as the school-level operational lead for technology management

Partner with the regional Technology team to ensure the ongoing management of all staff and student technology, including laptops and phones, and engage with external vendors to ensure the upkeep of building technology and equipment, including copiers, printers and WiFi
Be responsible for the security, monitoring and control of inventory and access to technology systems

Physical, Mental and Environmental Demands

Physical:

Ability to navigate both office and campus environments, and hold meetings in different spaces. Traditionally, much of the day involves sitting. Ability to access and utilize technology. Occasional lifting/carrying of equipment up to 20 lbs.

Mental:

Stress of deadlines and normal work standards, ability to analyze problems and generate alternatives, work with interruptions, concentrate for long periods of time, read, calculate, perform routine math problems, memorize and recall objects and people.

Environmental:

Office environment subject to constant interruptions and distractions. KIPP adheres to health and safety guidelines as outlined by the CDC, CDE, and public health agencies’ recommendations.

Classification

Full-time, exempt position

About KIPP Public Schools Northern California

We are a thriving nonprofit network of free, public charter schools open to all students. At KIPP, we believe all children should grow up free to create the future they want for themselves and that schools can and should be a critical factor in making that vision a reality. Together with families and communities, we create joyful, academically excellent schools that prepare students with the skills and confidence to pursue the paths they choose—college, career, and beyond—so they can lead fulfilling lives and build a more just world.

Our student community consists of over 7,000 elementary, middle, and high school students in East Palo Alto, Oakland, San Francisco, San Lorenzo, San Jose, Redwood City, and Stockton. 79% qualify for free or reduced price lunch, 23% are multilingual learners, and 10% have special needs. We strive to cultivate a representative team of teachers and leaders that reflect our students’ diversity.

Compensation

KIPP Northern California is dedicated to you and your family's well-being! We offer a competitive salary as well as a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, and transportation benefits.

We benchmark annually against comparably-sized non-profit organizations in the regions where we operate, to offer competitive salaries. The salary range for this position is between $72,485 - $83,178. Candidates are placed on our pay scale based on previous experience.

How to Apply

Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) Department

The EHS team is responsible for collaborating with Construction, Operations, Contractors, Vendors, and various regulatory agencies to ensure the health, safety, and environmental risks of the company are protected and that everyone enjoys a safe and healthful workplace. At Vantage, health, safety, and environmental protection are a core value that guides everything we do. By leveraging every individual that works at Vantage to lean into safety initiatives, and by executing the executive mandate that Vantage will place safety at the forefront of everything we do, our employees and those we work with enjoy a safety culture that is deeply ingrained and expects excellence in safety. This excellence is achieved through constant vigilance, planning, training, measurement, and cooperation, all of which is aligned with operational and construction activities and goals.

Position Overview

This role can be remote or based in any of our US locations: Denver, CO; Phoenix, AZ; Quincy, WA; Santa Clara, CA; or Ashburn, VA.

The EHS Program Manager is responsible for coordinating and driving execution across the A&E portfolio of strategic initiatives. This role serves as the point of integration between functional strategy, project execution, business partnership, and workstream owners.

Working directly with the global EHS team, the Program Manager will translate strategic priorities into executable roadmaps, establish timelines, coordinate dependencies, monitor progress, and ensure accountability across multiple concurrent initiatives. The role does not own the technical or functional work itself, but instead ensures the right people, priorities, resources, and milestones remain aligned to deliver outcomes for the business.

Portfolio & Program Management

Convert strategic objectives into structured work plans, milestones, timelines, and deliverables.

Workstream Coordination

Coordinate execution across multiple workstream owners and subject matter experts.

Track commitments, decisions, actions, and deliverables.
Escalate barriers, delays, and risks to leadership when appropriate.
Ensure initiatives remain aligned to agreed scope, timelines, and business objectives.

Administration & Governance

Serve as the A&E team's primary power user and administrator of the project management software.
Design and maintain project templates, portfolios, dashboards, reporting structures, automations, and workflows.
Develop metrics and reporting that provide visibility into progress, workload, risks, and resource utilization.
Continuously improve project management processes through system optimization and automation.

Organizational Partnership

Act as the primary coordination point between A&E and business-sponsored programs.
Align A&E deliverables with broader organizational priorities and implementation schedules.
Support initiative planning, stakeholder engagement, communication planning, and execution readiness activities.
Work closely with portfolio leaders and business partners to integrate A&E support into enterprise transformation efforts.

Additional Duties:

Lead or support special projects, transformation initiatives, and operational improvement efforts that advance the goals of the EHS and Adoption & Enablement functions.
Perform other duties as assigned, including supporting new business priorities, organizational initiatives, team events and meetings, and strategic efforts as the function continues to evolve.

Success in this role looks like:

Establish a single portfolio management framework across all A&E initiatives.
Create executive-level visibility into initiative status, risks, and resource needs.
Improve project delivery predictability and milestone achievement.
Enable workstream owners to focus on execution while ensuring accountability and coordination are maintained.

Job Requirements

Education:

Bachelor’s Degree in Environmental, Health and Safety or a related degree in Business, Project Management, Organizational Development, Operations, Engineering, or related field.

Experience:

5+ years of project, program, portfolio, or business operations management experience.
Demonstrated success managing complex, cross-functional programs with multiple stakeholders.
Experience building and managing program roadmaps and enterprise-level implementation plans.
Experience supporting organizational change, transformation, or operational improvement initiatives.
Experience working with executive leadership and cross-functional business teams in a matrixed organization.

Skills:

Advanced experience in project management software (such as ClickUp) required.
Strong proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, and SharePoint.
Experience building status reports and executive presentations.
Strong understanding of project management methodologies and techniques.
Strategic thinking with strong execution discipline.
Independent, self-directed, and highly organized.
Ability to manage complex, multi-track programs simultaneously.
Strong presence and communication skills in professional settings.
Operates effectively with ambiguity and change.
Familiarity with Procore & Power BI a plus.
Travel required is expected to be up to 5%.

Physical Demands And Special Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee may be required to stand; walk; sit; use hands to handle, or feel objects; reach with hands and arms; climb stairs or ladders; balance; stoop or kneel; talk and hear. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Walking construction sites with unlevel, uneven and/or rocky surfaces, as well as being outside in weather conditions that may include heat, cold, and wind, for brief periods of time may be required. The use of Personal Protective Equipment may also be required, including wearing a hardhat, safety glasses, hearing protection, safety toed shoes, and additional outerwear.

Additional Details

Salary Range: $115,000 - $125,000 Base + Bonus (this range is based on Colorado market data and may vary in other locations)
This position is eligible for company benefits including but not limited to medical, dental, and vision coverage, life and AD&D, short and long-term disability coverage, paid time off, employee assistance, participation in a 401k program that includes company match, and many other additional voluntary benefits.

We operate with No Ego and No Arrogance. We work to build each other up and support one another, appreciating each other’s strengths and respecting each other’s weaknesses. new_jobs.title: Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Who Are We?

Groundswell is a premier technology integrator and solution provider, resolutely committed to solving the most complex challenges facing federal agencies today. Our name, Groundswell, represents our commitment to be an unstoppable, seismic change in government. Ours is a small company culture with big company reach and results. Are you ready to be audacious, be bold and drive change at a rapid pace? Join us, where we’ll make a greater impact together.

What You'll do:

Groundswell is seeking an experienced Program Manager to lead the day-to-day management and execution of a flagship Intelligence Community modernization program. Reporting to the Executive Program Director, this individual will serve as the program’s operational leader, with responsibility for contract execution, program controls, customer coordination, financial performance, integrated schedule management, risk and dependency management, subcontractor performance, and coordination with OEM and government stakeholders.

While the Executive Program Manager provides executive oversight, strategic direction, and senior customer engagement, the Program Manager will be responsible for the daily operation and execution of the program. This individual will ensure Groundswell meets contractual requirements, Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) performance standards, milestones, deliverables, financial commitments, and customer expectations.

The Program Manager will work closely with the OEM Program Management Office (PMO) to manage cross-program dependencies, schedules, risks, and decisions that could impact Groundswell's delivery commitments. The Program Manager will also provide leadership and oversight to Groundswell's Workday Delivery Lead and other functional and technical workstream leaders, ensuring individual delivery efforts remain aligned with the overall program plan.

This role is designed to assume increasing program leadership responsibility as the program matures and transitions from initial implementation and establishment into steady-state program execution.

Key Responsibilities:

Program & Contract Execution

Lead the day-to-day execution and management of the task order under the strategic direction and executive oversight of the Executive Program Manager.
Manage compliance with contract terms, requirements, performance standards, and customer commitments.
Manage contractual deliverables, milestones, reporting requirements, and Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) performance measures.
Establish and maintain the program's operating cadence, governance processes, performance reporting, and management controls.
Ensure contract deliverables are completed, reviewed, submitted, and tracked through customer acceptance.
Coordinate across technical and functional workstreams to ensure execution remains aligned with contractual requirements and program objectives.
Serve as the primary escalation point for day-to-day program execution issues.

Integrated Schedule, Risk & Dependency Management

Develop, maintain, and manage the program Integrated Master Schedule (IMS), incorporating Groundswell, subcontractor, OEM, customer, and other external milestones and dependencies.
Lead program-level risk, issue, dependency, action, and decision management processes.
Identify cross-workstream and external dependencies that could affect program milestones, contractual commitments, cost, or performance.
Develop and drive mitigation and contingency plans for program-level risks and schedule impacts.
Coordinate with the Workday Delivery Lead and other workstream leaders to incorporate detailed delivery plans and milestones into the overall IMS.
Escalate significant risks, issues, decisions, and potential contractual impacts to the Executive Program Manager and government leadership as appropriate.

OEM & External Dependency Management

Serve as the primary day-to-day program management interface with the OEM PMO.
Coordinate schedules, milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, and decisions between Groundswell and the OEM program.
Assess changes to OEM plans and schedules for potential impacts to Groundswell's scope, IMS, resources, deliverables, and contractual milestones.
Drive timely resolution of cross-organizational dependencies and issues involving Groundswell, the OEM, subcontractors, and government stakeholders.
Maintain clear visibility into external dependencies and proactively communicate potential impacts to program leadership and the customer.

Financial & Contract Performance

Manage day-to-day program financial performance, including budgets, forecasts, staffing plans, burn rates, and cost performance.
Coordinate and oversee program invoicing activities to ensure accurate and timely billing in accordance with contractual requirements.
Monitor actual and forecasted performance against program financial objectives and identify potential variances.
Partner with Groundswell contracts, finance, and corporate leadership to address financial and contractual issues.
Provide the Executive Program Manager with regular visibility into program financial health and areas requiring executive action.

Customer & Program Governance

Serve as a primary day-to-day interface with government program leadership and stakeholders.
Lead recurring program status reviews, schedule reviews, risk reviews, performance reviews, and other program governance forums.
Prepare and deliver program-level reporting covering schedule, contractual performance, financials, staffing, risks, dependencies, deliverables, and required decisions.
Support the Executive Program Manager in executive-level customer engagements, strategic discussions, and escalations.
Build trusted relationships with government stakeholders through transparency, responsiveness, and disciplined program execution.

Team, Subcontractor & Delivery Oversight

Provide operational leadership across Groundswell's technical, functional, cybersecurity, program management, and operational workstreams.
Provide management oversight to the Workday Delivery Lead and other workstream leaders while maintaining clear accountability for their respective areas of delivery.
Manage subcontractor performance at the program level, including contractual commitments, staffing, schedules, deliverables, dependencies, and overall performance.
Coordinate with subcontractor leadership to resolve performance issues and maintain alignment with program requirements.
Ensure delivery teams have the priorities, resources, decisions, and support necessary to meet program commitments.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, transparency, customer focus, and delivery excellence.

Executive Program Manager Partnership

Serve as the principal deputy to the Executive Program Manager and act on their behalf for day-to-day program execution.
Maintain continuous visibility for the Executive Program Manager into program health, customer concerns, financial performance, contractual matters, risks, and decisions requiring executive attention.
Translate executive program direction into actionable plans and ensure execution across the program organization.
Assume program leadership responsibilities when delegated by the Executive Program Manager.
Support the evolution of program governance, operating models, and leadership responsibilities as the program matures.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in information systems, Engineering, Business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification required. Equivalent certification, such as DAWIA Level Three in Program Management, may be acceptable.
10+ years of experience managing complex Federal technology programs, task orders, or enterprise system implementations.
Experience supporting Intelligence Community (IC) and/or Department of Defense (DoD) programs.
Demonstrated experience managing Federal contract requirements, deliverables, performance measures, and customer commitments.
Demonstrated experience developing and managing Integrated Master Schedules (IMS), program-level risks, issues, dependencies, and corrective actions.
Experience managing program financials, including budgets, forecasts, staffing, cost performance, and invoicing.
Experience coordinating complex dependencies across government customers, OEMs, subcontractors, and delivery organizations.
Experience managing subcontractor and vendor performance in Federal or other highly regulated environments.
Strong leadership, communication, executive presentation, organization, and relationship management skills.
Demonstrated ability to operate independently, make sound program decisions, and appropriately escalate risks, issues, and decisions in a complex customer environment.
Must be a US Citizen per contract requirements
Active Top Secret (TS) clearance required with the ability to obtain and maintain TS/SCI access and Counter Intelligence (CI) Polygraph. Candidates who currently hold an active TS/SCI clearance with CI Polygraph will receive priority consideration.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience managing large-scale enterprise ERP or HCM implementations, preferably Workday.
Experience supporting Intelligence Community programs within highly secure customer environments.
Experience coordinating program schedules, milestones, risks, and dependencies with an OEM or external Program Management Office (PMO).
Experience managing contract performance against Quality Assurance Surveillance Plans (QASPs), Service Level Agreements (SLAs), or similar performance standards.
Experience with Earned Value Management (EVM), cost and schedule performance analysis, and program forecasting.
Experience supporting programs through Risk Management Framework (RMF) and Authority to Operate (ATO) processes.
Familiarity with the Workday implementation lifecycle and methodology.

Work Location & Travel Requirements

Must be local to the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area and willing to work onsite within customer SCIF environments a minimum of four (4) days per week.
Approximately 5% travel within the Washington, D.C., Maryland, and Virginia (DMV) region is required.
Occasional non-standard work hours may be required to support mission and program needs.

Skills:

Certification:

Project Management Professional (PMP)® Certification - PMI

Why You’ll Never Want to Leave:

Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans
Flexible Spending Account
4% 401K Match (immediate vesting)
Paid Time Off
Tuition reimbursement, certification programs, and professional development
Flexible work schedule
On-site gym and childcare option

$183,760.00 - $308,181.00

When you care deeply about the work you do, it’s rewarding to see it through from concept to completion. We partner with clients to provide both program management and construction management to strategize, plan, and implement projects that drive organizations forward. From hospitals and airports to university campuses, mass transit systems, water treatment facilities, mines, and wind farms, we've successfully managed thousands of projects. 

Joining our team, turning visionary ideas into reality, will shape your future—and the future of your community.

We are strategizing, planning, and implementing projects that help clients achieve their organization’s objectives. Join our award-winning program management team and bring transformational project solutions to life.

Your Opportunity

Stantec is seeking a Senior Project Manager (PM) to join our Program and Construction Management team. The PM ensures the success of assigned projects through client engagement, leadership and team management. You will focus on providing strategic advice and leadership oversight to project/program activities, expectations, and risk, while leading, supporting, and/or advising clients throughout all stages of the project life cycle. You will have a sound knowledge of the construction industry, project management functions, tools and systems and be able to prioritize and work on multiple projects simultaneously.

Your Key Responsibilities

Directly deliver or oversee others delivering projects and programs for Stantec’s clients that are in alignment with client expectations on quality, budget and schedule.
Obtain a solid understanding and working competency of Stantec technical systems and business processes.
Actively advise on diverse capital projects of varying size and complexity across any of the Stantec sectors.
Inspire confidence with stakeholders and the project team with your project management skills and leadership abilities.
Provide oversight on the performance of the project team and provide coaching, mentoring and leadership as required.
Engage with clients and obtain client feedback on our performance.
Raise our team’s profile in the industry and help establish your reputation as an expert within Stantec. This includes presenting at conferences or events.
Contribute in the development the annual business plan and budget for the team, as required.
Assist in team engagement and morale that is demonstrated by incremental improvement in corporate team survey results.
Assist in resource management, recruitment, and succession planning to support the growth of our team.
Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and the HSE management system on assigned projects.

Your Capabilities and Credentials

Involvement on projects delivered under a wide range of procurement methods (including DB, PDB, P3, CM etc.) is an asset.
Strong leadership skills & the ability to move a team forward, especially with leading a team of project managers and overseeing the delivery of their work with consistency in approach and quality.
Strong collaboration skills, capable of bringing multiple team members from different business lines together to successfully manage multi-disciplinary projects and programs.
Ability to manage project stakeholders by speaking clearly and persuasively with exceptional interpersonal skills.
Detail-oriented, dependable, and able to perform well under the pressure of deadlines.
Adapts to a dynamic project environment and able to manage multiple tasks over an extended period.
Solid verbal and written communication skills.
Proactively Identifies project risks and determines their impact on the project with a proven ability to mitigate or resolve in a timely manner.
Demonstrated ability to work successfully with clients, internal teams and contractors.
Strong computer literacy in scheduling, word processing, presentation and spreadsheet software.
Experience with budget management in a package or custom software.
Strong understanding of design and construction process and requirements.
Understanding of plans, contracts and specifications.
Exceptional organizational skills and problem-solving abilities.
Believes in developing trust and relationship with the project team based on performance

Education and Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Architecture, Engineering, Construction Management, or a similar field would be an asset.
8 years of experience across varying sectors, project scales, and complexities.
Experience in leading and managing various project teams.
An equivalent combination of education and experience in a related field may substitute for education only.
P.Eng, PMP certification, or an equivalent designation would be an asset.

Title: Staff Program Manager

Job Function: Engineering

Location: PDC

Workplace Category: Onsite

Company: Harley-Davidson Motor Company

Full or Part-Time: Full Time

Shift: SHIFT1

In 1903, out of a small shed in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, four young men lit a cultural wildfire that would grow and spread across geographies and generations. Their innovation and imagination for what was possible on two wheels sparked a transportation revolution that would make Harley-Davidson the most recognizable motorcycle brand in the world. Today, we continue to define motorcycle culture, evoking soul-stirring emotion reflected in every product and experience we deliver - like we have for well over a century and will for generations to come. Are you ready to ride with us?

The Harley-Davidson Motor Company Product Development Center (PDC) located in Wauwatosa, WI is home to the mantra – You dream it. We build it. Join our team as a Staff Program Manager.

Job Summary

The Staff Product Development Technical Program Manager owns program operations and leads project teams in all phases of H-D motorcycle product development including planning, design, verification, production validation, and production launch. The Technical Program Manager works within the Product Line Engineering (PLE) team and serves as the expert in program execution while partnering with the Product Line Engineering Manager to remove barriers and focus teams on what is most critical to deliver value to the customer.

This Role

Owns motorcycle and accessory program/project health
Manages program targets, requirements, and approvals
Executes program to deliver requirements and metrics for success
Builds strong connections with cross-functional peers
Creates clarity to enable empowered program decisions
A vocal advocate for the Program Leadership Team & Quality & CI

Job Responsibilities

WHAT You Do

Critical Path Plan:
Establish, manage, and drive the program-level critical path via a deep understanding of crucial deliverables and cross-functional timing interdependencies (e.g. design and tooling release dates, supplier selection, build events, etc.). Provide options to maintain program timing and health when faced with challenges. Use previous program & design delivery experience to draw the critical path and interdependencies from other people’s plans.

Risk & Issue Management:
Leverage technical knowledge to actively identify program-level risks & issues and steps to mitigate. Ensure cross-functional alignment on risks & issues with program implications understood, clear ownership, effective prioritization and actions that efficiently drive resolution.

Resource Management:
Own the resource management process for the program. Monitor health and identify issues that affect the program through its duration.

Metrics:

Responsibilities/Qualifications

The Senior Technical Project Manager
will be responsible for directly managing or overseeing a wide range of NextGen 911 Public Safety deployment project types. Deployment types may include PSAP (911 Call Center) deployment projects; carrier interoperability evaluation and testing; equipment vendor interoperability evaluation and testing, and new feature evaluation and testing in partnership with partners, product, and development teams.

This position will be responsible for partner and/or customer coordination and management, internal resource and provisioning management, creating project plans, evaluating, and documenting current and new processes, and assisting the proposals and sales team with content related to winning new customers or partners. new_jobs.title: Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Who Are We?

Groundswell is a premier technology integrator and solution provider, resolutely committed to solving the most complex challenges facing federal agencies today. Our name, Groundswell, represents our commitment to be an unstoppable, seismic change in government. Ours is a small company culture with big company reach and results. Are you ready to be audacious, be bold and drive change at a rapid pace? Join us, where we’ll make a greater impact together.

What You'll do:

Groundswell is seeking an experienced Program Manager to lead the day-to-day management and execution of a flagship Intelligence Community modernization program. Reporting to the Executive Program Director, this individual will serve as the program’s operational leader, with responsibility for contract execution, program controls, customer coordination, financial performance, integrated schedule management, risk and dependency management, subcontractor performance, and coordination with OEM and government stakeholders.

While the Executive Program Manager provides executive oversight, strategic direction, and senior customer engagement, the Program Manager will be responsible for the daily operation and execution of the program. This individual will ensure Groundswell meets contractual requirements, Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) performance standards, milestones, deliverables, financial commitments, and customer expectations.

The Program Manager will work closely with the OEM Program Management Office (PMO) to manage cross-program dependencies, schedules, risks, and decisions that could impact Groundswell's delivery commitments. The Program Manager will also provide leadership and oversight to Groundswell's Workday Delivery Lead and other functional and technical workstream leaders, ensuring individual delivery efforts remain aligned with the overall program plan.

This role is designed to assume increasing program leadership responsibility as the program matures and transitions from initial implementation and establishment into steady-state program execution.

Key Responsibilities:

Program & Contract Execution

Lead the day-to-day execution and management of the task order under the strategic direction and executive oversight of the Executive Program Manager.
Manage compliance with contract terms, requirements, performance standards, and customer commitments.
Manage contractual deliverables, milestones, reporting requirements, and Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) performance measures.
Establish and maintain the program's operating cadence, governance processes, performance reporting, and management controls.
Ensure contract deliverables are completed, reviewed, submitted, and tracked through customer acceptance.
Coordinate across technical and functional workstreams to ensure execution remains aligned with contractual requirements and program objectives.
Serve as the primary escalation point for day-to-day program execution issues.

Integrated Schedule, Risk & Dependency Management

Develop, maintain, and manage the program Integrated Master Schedule (IMS), incorporating Groundswell, subcontractor, OEM, customer, and other external milestones and dependencies.
Lead program-level risk, issue, dependency, action, and decision management processes.
Identify cross-workstream and external dependencies that could affect program milestones, contractual commitments, cost, or performance.
Develop and drive mitigation and contingency plans for program-level risks and schedule impacts.
Coordinate with the Workday Delivery Lead and other workstream leaders to incorporate detailed delivery plans and milestones into the overall IMS.
Escalate significant risks, issues, decisions, and potential contractual impacts to the Executive Program Manager and government leadership as appropriate.

OEM & External Dependency Management

Serve as the primary day-to-day program management interface with the OEM PMO.
Coordinate schedules, milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, and decisions between Groundswell and the OEM program.
Assess changes to OEM plans and schedules for potential impacts to Groundswell's scope, IMS, resources, deliverables, and contractual milestones.
Drive timely resolution of cross-organizational dependencies and issues involving Groundswell, the OEM, subcontractors, and government stakeholders.
Maintain clear visibility into external dependencies and proactively communicate potential impacts to program leadership and the customer.

Financial & Contract Performance

Manage day-to-day program financial performance, including budgets, forecasts, staffing plans, burn rates, and cost performance.
Coordinate and oversee program invoicing activities to ensure accurate and timely billing in accordance with contractual requirements.
Monitor actual and forecasted performance against program financial objectives and identify potential variances.
Partner with Groundswell contracts, finance, and corporate leadership to address financial and contractual issues.
Provide the Executive Program Manager with regular visibility into program financial health and areas requiring executive action.

Customer & Program Governance

Serve as a primary day-to-day interface with government program leadership and stakeholders.
Lead recurring program status reviews, schedule reviews, risk reviews, performance reviews, and other program governance forums.
Prepare and deliver program-level reporting covering schedule, contractual performance, financials, staffing, risks, dependencies, deliverables, and required decisions.
Support the Executive Program Manager in executive-level customer engagements, strategic discussions, and escalations.
Build trusted relationships with government stakeholders through transparency, responsiveness, and disciplined program execution.

Team, Subcontractor & Delivery Oversight

Provide operational leadership across Groundswell's technical, functional, cybersecurity, program management, and operational workstreams.
Provide management oversight to the Workday Delivery Lead and other workstream leaders while maintaining clear accountability for their respective areas of delivery.
Manage subcontractor performance at the program level, including contractual commitments, staffing, schedules, deliverables, dependencies, and overall performance.
Coordinate with subcontractor leadership to resolve performance issues and maintain alignment with program requirements.
Ensure delivery teams have the priorities, resources, decisions, and support necessary to meet program commitments.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, transparency, customer focus, and delivery excellence.

Executive Program Manager Partnership

Serve as the principal deputy to the Executive Program Manager and act on their behalf for day-to-day program execution.
Maintain continuous visibility for the Executive Program Manager into program health, customer concerns, financial performance, contractual matters, risks, and decisions requiring executive attention.
Translate executive program direction into actionable plans and ensure execution across the program organization.
Assume program leadership responsibilities when delegated by the Executive Program Manager.
Support the evolution of program governance, operating models, and leadership responsibilities as the program matures.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in information systems, Engineering, Business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification required. Equivalent certification, such as DAWIA Level Three in Program Management, may be acceptable.
10+ years of experience managing complex Federal technology programs, task orders, or enterprise system implementations.
Experience supporting Intelligence Community (IC) and/or Department of Defense (DoD) programs.
Demonstrated experience managing Federal contract requirements, deliverables, performance measures, and customer commitments.
Demonstrated experience developing and managing Integrated Master Schedules (IMS), program-level risks, issues, dependencies, and corrective actions.
Experience managing program financials, including budgets, forecasts, staffing, cost performance, and invoicing.
Experience coordinating complex dependencies across government customers, OEMs, subcontractors, and delivery organizations.
Experience managing subcontractor and vendor performance in Federal or other highly regulated environments.
Strong leadership, communication, executive presentation, organization, and relationship management skills.
Demonstrated ability to operate independently, make sound program decisions, and appropriately escalate risks, issues, and decisions in a complex customer environment.
Must be a US Citizen per contract requirements
Active Top Secret (TS) clearance required with the ability to obtain and maintain TS/SCI access and Counter Intelligence (CI) Polygraph. Candidates who currently hold an active TS/SCI clearance with CI Polygraph will receive priority consideration.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience managing large-scale enterprise ERP or HCM implementations, preferably Workday.
Experience supporting Intelligence Community programs within highly secure customer environments.
Experience coordinating program schedules, milestones, risks, and dependencies with an OEM or external Program Management Office (PMO).
Experience managing contract performance against Quality Assurance Surveillance Plans (QASPs), Service Level Agreements (SLAs), or similar performance standards.
Experience with Earned Value Management (EVM), cost and schedule performance analysis, and program forecasting.
Experience supporting programs through Risk Management Framework (RMF) and Authority to Operate (ATO) processes.
Familiarity with the Workday implementation lifecycle and methodology.

Work Location & Travel Requirements

Must be local to the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area and willing to work onsite within customer SCIF environments a minimum of four (4) days per week.
Approximately 5% travel within the Washington, D.C., Maryland, and Virginia (DMV) region is required.
Occasional non-standard work hours may be required to support mission and program needs.

Skills:

Certification:

Project Management Professional (PMP)® Certification - PMI

Why You’ll Never Want to Leave:

Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans
Flexible Spending Account
4% 401K Match (immediate vesting)
Paid Time Off
Tuition reimbursement, certification programs, and professional development
Flexible work schedule
On-site gym and childcare option

new_jobs.description:
About Coresite

At CoreSite, we empower a more connected future through high-performance data centers and interconnection solutions. Recognized as a trusted partner in digital transformation, our strategically located facilities and innovative services enable businesses to connect, collaborate, and grow in an ever-evolving technological landscape.
Our culture is defined by operational excellence and a relentless drive for innovation. We foster a collaborative environment where every team member is valued, wins are celebrated as a team, and ownership is part of our DNA. At CoreSite, we’re not just building state-of-the-art infrastructure—we’re creating a community of forward-thinkers committed to solving complex challenges and delivering exceptional customer experiences.
At CoreSite not only are we Committed to Excellence, but we also Build Connections, Own It, Do the Right Thing, Have Fun, and Win as a Team. Join us and be part of a team that is shaping the future of digital infrastructure while nurturing your professional growth and success.
Project Manager / Scrum Master Role:

We are seeking a motivated Project Manager / Scrum Master to join our dynamic and growing IT team. In this dual role, you will lead Agile ceremonies while overseeing project timelines and deliverables across all stages of the Software Delivery Life Cycle (SDLC), applying Agile, Iterative, or Waterfall frameworks as appropriate. The ideal candidate thrives in collaborative environments, brings a strong background in technology-driven projects, and excels in leadership and communication. You will guide teams to balance multiple goals and deadlines while keeping broader objectives in focus. This role involves close collaboration across departments to deliver projects of varying scope, risk, and complexity efficiently.  
Essential Functions: 

Oversee software delivery projects through all SDLC stages, leveraging project management expertise to align processes with Agile, Iterative, or Waterfall frameworks, and adapt strategies as needed to meet project objectives.
Ensure effective communication and alignment with all stakeholders, including executive leadership, clients, and cross-departmental teams, to facilitate seamless project delivery.
Guide and coach teams to align with project goals and agile practices, managing multiple priorities while fostering a culture of continuous improvement through retrospectives and effective risk management.
Develop and execute strategies that enhance project delivery, improve team velocity and product quality, and advance organizational objectives by optimizing project delivery tools and processes, including tools like Jira.
Actively manage resource allocation, ensuring that project teams have the necessary skills, tools, and capacity to meet project demands.
Proactively manage risks and issues with effective mitigation strategies, to improve project outcomes and team performance.
Ensure project deliverables meet quality standards and are completed on time and within budget.
Coordinate internal and external dependencies, actively removing blockers to enhance team delivery effectiveness.
Assist with project intake and governance activities, including ROI calculations and benefits realization. 

Other Duties: 

Collaborate with leadership to monitor priorities, direction, and scope for the IT Roadmap. 
Lead and/or support RFP activities for new tool acquisition. 
Assist in conducting system, compliance, and process effectiveness audits, ensuring that project practices and team execution align with organizational and compliance standards. 
Support business continuity and disaster recovery update activities. 
Ensure project documentation is current, accessible, and well-maintained. 
Perform additional duties as assigned 

Requirements:

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities: 

Ability to thrive in a hybrid work environment that consists of at least two onsite days in downtown Denver office per week including Tuesdays and Wednesdays for in-person team collaboration 
Exceptional communication skills with the ability to engage at both technical and business levels. 
Strong documentation, problem-solving, and decision-making skills. 
Proficient in various project delivery tools like Jira, Confluence, and Rally. 
Adept at navigating ambiguity and connecting the dots to drive informed decisions. 
Ability to guide teams in adopting new technologies and processes. 
Strong understanding of software development processes, tools, and technologies (e.g., CI/CD pipelines, DevOps practices, cloud platforms) and how they enable efficient delivery of solutions. 
Familiarity with Agile scaling frameworks (e.g., SAFe, LeSS) for managing large and complex projects, desired. 
Strong conflict resolution and stakeholder management abilities, with a focus on fostering a positive, collaborative team environment. 
Critical thinking, analysis, and process improvement skills to drive continuous improvement in software delivery. 

Education/Experience: 

Bachelor’s degree in IT, computer science, project/program management, or a related field preferred. 
At least 4-6 years of experience in project management, including 3+ years leading technology projects and 2+ years supporting IT systems implementations. 
Experience with Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) packages (e.g., Salesforce, MuleSoft) is a preferred. 
PMP and/or CSM certification strongly preferred, with a demonstrated commitment to ongoing professional development.

While performing the job’s duties, the employee is occasionally required to stand; walk; sit; use hands to handle, or feel objects; reach with hands and arms; climb stairs; balance; stoop or kneel; talk and hear. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move objects weighing up to 25 pounds.

new_jobs.title: Senior Project Manager, Market Operations
new_jobs.description:
About Carvana

At Carvana, we sell cars, but we are not salespeople. We have made it our mission to create a hassle-free way for people to buy and sell cars. We saw a huge problem with how much of a headache it is to buy a car the traditional way, so we committed ourselves to put customer satisfaction at the core of our business, we have built a no-pressure, no-haggle online car buying experience that saves our customers time and money. Customers can search through thousands of vehicles online, see full 360-degree views of both the interior and exterior of the vehicles before deciding to go through the purchasing process. Our Customer Advocates will then either deliver the purchased vehicle to our customer’s driveway using one of our kick-ass one car haulers, or they will meet our customers at one of our amazing coin-operated Vending Machines.

About The Team And Position

Carvana’s Market Operation department is known for its team-oriented, fast-paced environment.

We expect bright people, willing to roll up their sleeves, take on new assignments, mentor and train others, assume additional responsibilities as needed while juggling multiple projects. Don’t forget to bring your personality! We thrive from each unique perspective. Our strength is in our diversity of opinions.

What You’ll Be Doing

Lead multiple high-priority initiatives and projects by successfully collaborating, communicating and prioritizing across essential stakeholders to ensure goals are achieved.
Build strong relationships and work cross-functionally (internally and externally) with the necessary partners to support project initiatives.
Successfully execute full-cycle project management duties to meet project goals within given constraints (define goal, scope, deliverables, resources, budget and timeline; planning, monitoring and controlling during execution and finally, closing), with minimal guidance.
Leverage advanced analytical skills to measure project success, assess operational performance, conduct root cause analysis, and develop data-driven recommendations that optimize performance and influence senior leadership decision-making.
Effectively work through areas of ambiguity and complexity; demonstrating initiative and structuring problem-solving approaches to achieve our business needs.
Dive deep into operations and leverage a strong understanding of Market Operations, performance metrics, and operational drivers to develop scalable solutions.
Identify operational weaknesses and risks, and help innovate or improve processes.
Use data to make operational decisions, uncover insights, and provide direction to senior management.
Train and coach teams on best-in-class project management methodologies, data-driven decision-making, and analytical frameworks.
Effectively partner with stakeholders to determine the needs of their departments and create/deliver communication plans to leadership; build, maintain, and communicate portfolio and/or project performance and progress across Market Operations platform and stakeholders.
Other duties as assigned

What You Should Have

Bachelor’s degree required and a minimum of 5 years working experience in Project Management, operations, business analytics, or a related role, ideally in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.
Experience leading cross-functional project teams through Initiation, Design, Planning, Execution and Close phases for large-scale, complex and ambiguous initiatives
Experience working across different business units (specifically HR, IT/technology, construction, engineering, procurement, operations) to communicate project vision, develop plans and drive change
Ability to structure and conduct root cause analysis, identify key performance indicators (KPIs), and develop effective solutions to operational challenges.
Strong analytical mindset with the ability to transform complex data sets into actionable insights and drive strategic decision-making.
Proficiency in Excel or Google Sheets for data analysis is required; experience retrieving data using Snowflake or SQL is preferred; familiarity with Tableau or other data visualization tools is also preferred.
Self-starter attitude with the ability to drive excellence and meet high standards
Fast learner with the ability to make decisions, problem solve, prioritize, and multi-task in an analytical and organized manner
Superior interpersonal skills, ability to interface with a variety of personalities with professionalism
Ability to take an entrepreneurial approach to project management and commitment to team support
Ability to learn quickly, transfer knowledge and provide valuable and actionable feedback
Ability to manage multiple projects at the same time while maintaining high attention to detail
Must be willing to travel when necessary (up to 10% of the time)

What We’ll Offer In Return

Full-Time Salary Position.
Medical, Dental, and Vision benefits.
401K with company match.
A multitude of perks including student loan payments, discounts on vehicles, benefits for your pets, and much more.
A great wellness program to keep you healthy and happy both physically and mentally.
Access to opportunities to expand your skill set and share your knowledge with others across the organization.
A company culture of promotions from within, with a start-up atmosphere allowing for varied and rapid career development.
A seat in one of the fastest-growing companies in the country.

Other Requirements

To be able to do your job at Carvana, there are some basic requirements we want to share with you.

Must be able to read, write, speak, and understand English.
The ability to walk/stand and sustain physical activity for extended periods of time (8+ hours).
Must be able to stay in stationary positions for extended periods of time (when driving) up to 3 hours at a time.
Frequently communicates with customers and must be able to exchange accurate information.

Of course, we’ll make any reasonable accommodations for those with disabilities to perform the essential functions of their jobs.

Legal stuff

Hiring is contingent on passing a complete background check. This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

new_jobs.title: Senior Intelligence Analyst - Threat Management Unit
new_jobs.description:
Overview

The newly established Threat Management Unit (TMU), as part of a greater NFCU Global Security team, is hiring a Senior Intelligence Analyst to help buildout and lead a broader intelligence-driven capability focused on proactively identifying, assessing, and mitigating threats across cyber, physical, and human domains. This position is critical in modernizing and innovating the TMU intelligence function by working complex OSINT-driven analysis, supporting a broad range of insider threat investigations, identifying counterintelligence opportunities, and mitigating an array of sophisticated threats targeting Navy Federal. Working in a highly collaborative environment, this analyst partners across the organization to enhance threat detection, risk identification, and response capabilities, while fusing behavioral, technical, and investigative intelligence into a unified threat picture and delivering clear, actionable insights. The role provides direct analytical support across key Global Security teams, including Investigations, Insider Threat, Counterintelligence, Executive Protection, and Physical Security Operations.

Responsibilities

Lead and direct the Intelligence Analysis team, setting analytic priorities, standards, and workflows to support Navy Federal security and investigative missions.
Lead complex investigations and advanced threat assessments
Identify and assess sophisticated threat patterns impacting personnel and operations
Mentor junior analysts and provide guidance on analytic methodologies
Develop and present executive-level intelligence briefings
Support protective intelligence and executive protection initiatives
Conduct all-source intelligence analysis focused on security risks
Collect, validate, and analyze open-source, social media, and proprietary data
Apply structured analytic techniques to support investigative assessments
Develop clear, actionable intelligence products and brief stakeholders
Collaborate with internal partners for case resolution and preventive measures
Assist with basic open-source and proprietary research under supervision
Support data collection and validation for security investigations
Identify threat indicators and anomalies
Track investigative tasks, workflows, deadlines, and performance metrics using basic project management and reporting tools

Advanced Skills And Proficiencies

Demonstrated experience conducting intelligence analysis supporting investigations & operations using a variety information sources and analytic methodologies
Proven ability to perform OSINT-driven investigative research with high accuracy, discretion, and attention to detail
Strong analytical writing and briefing skills, with the ability to translate complex data into clear, actionable security assessments
Experience applying structured analytic techniques and critical thinking to intelligence or investigative problem sets
Familiarity with digital investigations, online attribution, social media exploitation, and research methodologies
Ability to work independently, manage sensitive information, and operate effectively in a corporate security environment

Qualifications

5+ years of experience as an Analyst in Intelligence or Corporate Security
Bachelor’s degree or relevant coursework in security, intelligence, or related field or the equivalent combination of education, training or experience
Experience supporting corporate security, insider threat programs, fraud investigations, or enterprise risk management
Prior collaboration with cross-functional partners such as Legal, Compliance, Risk, and Employee Relations teams
Experience working within an Intelligence Community (IC), law enforcement, military intelligence, or corporate security organization

Desired Qualifications

10+ years of experience in All-Source Intelligence Analyst, Corporate Security Analyst, or Investigations Analyst
Master’s degree in intelligence, security studies, criminal justice, psychology, or related discipline
Active or prior security clearance
USG intelligence analysis training and experience, including the use of classified systems and analytical programs
Professional certifications such Certified Threat Manager (CTM), Certified Protection Professional (CPP), etc.

As a Project Manager, you will work closely with multiple teams within Bosch as well as clients and subcontractors to, scope, plan and build highly complex projects using the latest technology from the best vendors, including Lenel, Genetec, Axis, Milestone and Avigilon. Tasked with managing every aspect, from start to finish, of our major projects for new construction, you are responsible for delivering high-quality project results.

You will manage the project team as efficiently as possible while representing the company in a professional manner in line with our values of a leadership mindset, people development, team, and client focused. Past experience managing large, multi-million-dollar projects will be a strong asset for this position. Stakeholder engagement across complex organizations and within Paladin will be an important part of this role as well.

Responsibilities

Develop and manage schedules for on-time delivery, monitor budgets to control costs and maintain financial health
Develop and manage project plan: includes plans for client communication expectations, project resource requirements and availability, procurement and management of materials and reconciliation, project commissioning, development of risk management and mitigation strategies, scheduling to ensure efficiency, in-depth knowledge and understanding of stakeholders expectations and requirements
Provide accurate financial reports for performance targets to meet the desired profit margin
Develop and maintain long-term client relationships that lead to repeat business and business development opportunities
Create documentation and ensure it clear, easy to follow, updated as per communication schedule, and accessible to all stakeholders
Control costs and maximize productivity through the implementation of best practices and standard processes
Effectively manage and maintain all written and verbal project communications, both formal and informal
Maintain client satisfaction and promptly resolve any concerns
Develop relationships with subcontractors to build a pool of resources; manage selection of subcontracts for projects, where required
Proactively assess risks; ensure a safe and healthy work environment

Supervisor Duties

In accordance with applicable Company policies/procedures and Federal/State laws, will perform the following supervisory responsibilities: planning, assigning, and directing work; coaching and appraising performance; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complaints and resolving problems.

3+ years of experience in an administrative role, project management, security integration or technical experience all in a security system or a system integration environment

Strong computer skills, with proficiency in Microsoft Office and project software
Able to work independently, manage time effectively, and work with multiple deadlines

Associate's degree (2 year) or bachelor's degree (4 year) in a technical capacity.

The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and may be required to work at heights over 1.8m (6 feet)

Working Conditions

This is a business-led
implementation programme. You will design the business processes from the ground up and make sure they are effectively implemented in SAP and connected digital systems. Scope

The initial focus is the end-to-end Order-to-Cash
process:

Sales and order management
Product costing
Logistics and delivery
Commercial processes
Invoicing and settlement

The role also covers related processes:

Procurement
Material handling and inventory transactions
Production-related processes
Quality and material movements
Master data, integrations and interfaces with production-adjacent systems

Responsibilities

Lead the programme from planning and process design through implementation, testing, deployment and stabilisation.
Coordinate business functions, process owners, subject matter experts, digital teams, architects, vendors and implementation partners.
Lead workshops and drive alignment on new business processes and procedures.
Ensure processes work seamlessly across operations, sales, logistics, procurement, finance and commercial functions.
Manage scope, priorities, dependencies, risks, decisions, resources and milestones.

More than 10 years of relevant experience.

Experience managing implementation partners, risks, dependencies, testing activities and delivery governance.

Experience with SAP S/4HANA (an advantage, but not essential).

Responsibilities / Essential Job Function

new_jobs.title: Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Who Are We?

Groundswell is a premier technology integrator and solution provider, resolutely committed to solving the most complex challenges facing federal agencies today. Our name, Groundswell, represents our commitment to be an unstoppable, seismic change in government. Ours is a small company culture with big company reach and results. Are you ready to be audacious, be bold and drive change at a rapid pace? Join us, where we’ll make a greater impact together.

What You'll do:

Groundswell is seeking an experienced Program Manager to lead the day-to-day management and execution of a flagship Intelligence Community modernization program. Reporting to the Executive Program Director, this individual will serve as the program’s operational leader, with responsibility for contract execution, program controls, customer coordination, financial performance, integrated schedule management, risk and dependency management, subcontractor performance, and coordination with OEM and government stakeholders.

While the Executive Program Manager provides executive oversight, strategic direction, and senior customer engagement, the Program Manager will be responsible for the daily operation and execution of the program. This individual will ensure Groundswell meets contractual requirements, Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) performance standards, milestones, deliverables, financial commitments, and customer expectations.

The Program Manager will work closely with the OEM Program Management Office (PMO) to manage cross-program dependencies, schedules, risks, and decisions that could impact Groundswell's delivery commitments. The Program Manager will also provide leadership and oversight to Groundswell's Workday Delivery Lead and other functional and technical workstream leaders, ensuring individual delivery efforts remain aligned with the overall program plan.

This role is designed to assume increasing program leadership responsibility as the program matures and transitions from initial implementation and establishment into steady-state program execution.

Key Responsibilities:

Program & Contract Execution

Lead the day-to-day execution and management of the task order under the strategic direction and executive oversight of the Executive Program Manager.
Manage compliance with contract terms, requirements, performance standards, and customer commitments.
Manage contractual deliverables, milestones, reporting requirements, and Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) performance measures.
Establish and maintain the program's operating cadence, governance processes, performance reporting, and management controls.
Ensure contract deliverables are completed, reviewed, submitted, and tracked through customer acceptance.
Coordinate across technical and functional workstreams to ensure execution remains aligned with contractual requirements and program objectives.
Serve as the primary escalation point for day-to-day program execution issues.

Integrated Schedule, Risk & Dependency Management

Develop, maintain, and manage the program Integrated Master Schedule (IMS), incorporating Groundswell, subcontractor, OEM, customer, and other external milestones and dependencies.
Lead program-level risk, issue, dependency, action, and decision management processes.
Identify cross-workstream and external dependencies that could affect program milestones, contractual commitments, cost, or performance.
Develop and drive mitigation and contingency plans for program-level risks and schedule impacts.
Coordinate with the Workday Delivery Lead and other workstream leaders to incorporate detailed delivery plans and milestones into the overall IMS.
Escalate significant risks, issues, decisions, and potential contractual impacts to the Executive Program Manager and government leadership as appropriate.

OEM & External Dependency Management

Serve as the primary day-to-day program management interface with the OEM PMO.
Coordinate schedules, milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, and decisions between Groundswell and the OEM program.
Assess changes to OEM plans and schedules for potential impacts to Groundswell's scope, IMS, resources, deliverables, and contractual milestones.
Drive timely resolution of cross-organizational dependencies and issues involving Groundswell, the OEM, subcontractors, and government stakeholders.
Maintain clear visibility into external dependencies and proactively communicate potential impacts to program leadership and the customer.

Financial & Contract Performance

Manage day-to-day program financial performance, including budgets, forecasts, staffing plans, burn rates, and cost performance.
Coordinate and oversee program invoicing activities to ensure accurate and timely billing in accordance with contractual requirements.
Monitor actual and forecasted performance against program financial objectives and identify potential variances.
Partner with Groundswell contracts, finance, and corporate leadership to address financial and contractual issues.
Provide the Executive Program Manager with regular visibility into program financial health and areas requiring executive action.

Customer & Program Governance

Serve as a primary day-to-day interface with government program leadership and stakeholders.
Lead recurring program status reviews, schedule reviews, risk reviews, performance reviews, and other program governance forums.
Prepare and deliver program-level reporting covering schedule, contractual performance, financials, staffing, risks, dependencies, deliverables, and required decisions.
Support the Executive Program Manager in executive-level customer engagements, strategic discussions, and escalations.
Build trusted relationships with government stakeholders through transparency, responsiveness, and disciplined program execution.

Team, Subcontractor & Delivery Oversight

Provide operational leadership across Groundswell's technical, functional, cybersecurity, program management, and operational workstreams.
Provide management oversight to the Workday Delivery Lead and other workstream leaders while maintaining clear accountability for their respective areas of delivery.
Manage subcontractor performance at the program level, including contractual commitments, staffing, schedules, deliverables, dependencies, and overall performance.
Coordinate with subcontractor leadership to resolve performance issues and maintain alignment with program requirements.
Ensure delivery teams have the priorities, resources, decisions, and support necessary to meet program commitments.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, transparency, customer focus, and delivery excellence.

Executive Program Manager Partnership

Serve as the principal deputy to the Executive Program Manager and act on their behalf for day-to-day program execution.
Maintain continuous visibility for the Executive Program Manager into program health, customer concerns, financial performance, contractual matters, risks, and decisions requiring executive attention.
Translate executive program direction into actionable plans and ensure execution across the program organization.
Assume program leadership responsibilities when delegated by the Executive Program Manager.
Support the evolution of program governance, operating models, and leadership responsibilities as the program matures.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in information systems, Engineering, Business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification required. Equivalent certification, such as DAWIA Level Three in Program Management, may be acceptable.
10+ years of experience managing complex Federal technology programs, task orders, or enterprise system implementations.
Experience supporting Intelligence Community (IC) and/or Department of Defense (DoD) programs.
Demonstrated experience managing Federal contract requirements, deliverables, performance measures, and customer commitments.
Demonstrated experience developing and managing Integrated Master Schedules (IMS), program-level risks, issues, dependencies, and corrective actions.
Experience managing program financials, including budgets, forecasts, staffing, cost performance, and invoicing.
Experience coordinating complex dependencies across government customers, OEMs, subcontractors, and delivery organizations.
Experience managing subcontractor and vendor performance in Federal or other highly regulated environments.
Strong leadership, communication, executive presentation, organization, and relationship management skills.

Improve Dashboards and Reporting

Document important metrics, dashboards, tables, business definitions, and data owners.
Help identify outdated reporting logic and work with stakeholders to confirm how it should be updated.
Follow and contribute to standards for naming, documentation, validation, and data quality.
Help us understand how data is being consumed before reports, tables, or pipelines are changed.
Escalate data-quality and pipeline issues clearly to the appropriate technical owner.

Communicate and Collaborate
